title: IBM Security Bulletin: A security vulnerability has been identified in IBM WebSphere Application Server shipped with Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus WebGUI - United States
text:
SECURITY BULLETIN

SUMMARY
Websphere Application Server (WAS) is shipped as a component of Tivoli Netcool/OMNIbus WebGUI. Information about a security vulnerability affecting WAS has been published in a security bulletin.

VULNERABILITY DETAILS
Please consult the security bulletin Information disclosure in Remote code execution vulnerability in the JSF used by WebSphere Application Server [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=ibm10716525] for vulnerability details and information about fixes.

AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS


Principal Product and Version(s) Affected Supporting Product and Version WebGUI 7.4.0 GA and FP embedded Websphere Application Server 7.0 WebGUI 8.1.0 GA and FP Websphere Application Server 8.5 Please also note the end of support announcement [http://www.ibm.com/common/ssi/ShowDoc.wss?docURL=/common/ssi/rep_ca/8/897/ENUS917-138/index.html&lang=en&request_locale=en]from 12 September 2017 for selected Netcool product versions. You can find detailed information on whether the product version you have installed in your environment is affected by this end of service announcement by following the Netcool End of Support Knowledge Collection [https://www.ibm.com/support/entdocview.wss?uid=swg22009231]. If your product version is affected, IBM recommend to upgrade your product version to the latest supported version of your product. Please contact your IBM account manager for any question you might have or for any assistance you may require for upgrading an end of service announced offering. 

GET NOTIFIED ABOUT FUTURE SECURITY BULLETINS


Subscribe to My Notifications [ http://www-01.ibm.com/software/support/einfo.html] to be notified of important product support alerts like this.

REFERENCE
Complete CVSS v3 Guide [http://www.first.org/cvss/user-guide]
On-line Calculator v3 [http://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.0]

RELATED INFORMATION
IBM Secure Engineering Web Portal [http://www.ibm.com/security/secure-engineering/bulletins.html]
IBM Product Security Incident Response Blog [http://www.ibm.com/blogs/psirt]

ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
Vulnerability reported to IBM by dongyicheng

CHANGE HISTORY
21 August 2018: Original version published

*The CVSS Environment Score is customer environment specific and will ultimately impact the Overall CVSS Score. Customers can evaluate the impact of this vulnerability in their environments by accessing the links in the Reference section of this Security Bulletin.

DISCLAIMER

IBM PROVIDES THE CVSS SCORES ""AS IS"" WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. title: IBM Converting from IPAT - United States
text:
KnowledgeCollection TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Converting from IPAT 

ANSWER


 This document contains the procedures for converting from a traditional IPAT network to an IPAT with aliasing network, and for converting from IPAT with aliasing to a traditional network. This information applies to HACMP Enhanced Scalability 4.5 and higher and AIX 5.1 and higher. 




 CONVERTING FROM A TRADITIONAL IPAT NETWORK TO AN IPAT WITH ALIASING NETWORK (IPAT=IP ADDRESS TAKEOVER) 
 1. Stop the cluster on all nodes.  
    
    
 2.  Configure the existing service labels and boot interfaces for the network so that they use different subnets. This will require changes to both the HACMP and AIX configurations.  
    
    
 3.  On an HPS network, remove the old boot labels from the HA configuration and configure the base HPS adapter addresses as HACMP boot interfaces. For other network types, convert the existing standby interfaces into boot interfaces.  
    
    
 4.  Verify that the network is configured to support gratuitous ARP by checking the NIM settings for the network type.  
    
    
 5.  Ensure that the USE IP ALIASING FOR IPAT setting is not "disable". (smitty cm_config_nets_change_net.select or see options under Configure IP Based Networks SMIT screen)  
    
    
 6.  Synchronize the cluster topology. 




 CONVERTING FROM IPAT WITH ALIASING TO A TRADITIONAL NETWORK 
 1.  Stop the cluster on all nodes.  
    
    
 2.  If the network is using multiple boot interfaces on each node, convert all but one of them into standby interfaces, leaving just one boot interface per node on the network.  
    
    
 3.  Reconfigure the service labels so that they are on the same subnet as the remaining boot interfaces.  
    
    
 4.  Set the USE IP ALIASING FOR IPAT field to disable for the network.  
    
    
 5.  Synchronize the cluster topology.

text:

 *  In HOD when double clicking the mouse it doesn't generate AID
   ENTER except programmable Mouse Buttons ENPTUI Field.  When
   using the Programmable Mouse Buttons ENPTUI structure field data
   stream has the capability to define mouse double click.  Pcomm
   and maybe another application always sends ENTER on a Mouse
   double click.  The problem occurs when the double clicking in
   the ENPTUI selection list, this shouldn't be a Programmable

   ENTER to proceed.  This is the spec on HOD because HOD does not
   generate ENTER on double clicking.  Since it is reasonable and
   convenient to accept double clicking in ENPTUI fields, HOD

APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  idsideploy fails with the following errors:
   
   GLPIDL051W The replication configuration was not successful.
   The online backup of the source server will not be performed.
   
   GLPIDL053W The restore of the database was not successful or was
   not attempted due to a previous error.  For replication to be
   fully configured, the data must be loaded on the target
   directory server instance.
   
   From ibmslapd.log:
   
   2017-08-28T16:28:10.615072-4:00 GLPRPL036E Error 'simple bind:
   Can't contact LDAP server' occurred for replica 'CN=TEST.IBM.COM
   :2389,CN=IDSPEER1,IBM-REPLICAGROUP=DEFAULT,O=SAMPLE': bind
   failed using masterDn 'cn=replcred'.
   
   Note that the error:
   
   GLPIDL051W The replication configuration was not successful.
   The online backup of the source server will not be performed.
   
   Also indicates there is another idsdeploy defect that will be
   fixed under other APAR(s); you will need both this fix and the
   following fix to resolve idsidelpoy errors shown above.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX
 *  This error can be worked around be setting this environment
   variable in the ibmslapd.conf file:
   
   ibm-slapdSetenv: IBMLDAP_ATTR_INCLUDE_BINARY=FALSE
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  The root error here is the replica credentials password used the
   ;binary attribute option, and the SDS LDAP server was not
   parsing the replicaCredentials attribute name correctly, and as
   such was not correctly determining the credential password:
   
   cn=replcred,cn=replication,cn=IBMpolicies
   replicaCredentials;binary=secret
   replicaBindDN=cn=replcred
   
   When the LDAP server code was changed to handle the ;binary
   attribute option, changes were missed in the idsdeploy code.
   This APAR makes those missing changes.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The fix for this APAR will be contained in the following
   maintenance packages:
   | firmware upgrade | 8.0.1.4-ISS-ISDS_*.pkg |

title: IBM LI70667: ARCHIVE LIBRARY FILE NOT FOUND - United States
text:
A FIX IS AVAILABLE
Latest updates for XL C/C++ Advanced Edition V7 for Linux [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24009052]


SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  *** This APAR was originally reported on, and fixed on, another
   compiler platform. The following text is taken from the APAR for
   the original product and platform. This APAR has been fixed and
   is included in the February 2005 XL C/C++ Advanced Edition
   V7.0 for Linux Update. ***
   .
   ABSTRACT:         archive library file not found
   COMPILE COMMAND:  xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -c main.c
                     xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -c func.c
                     xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -G -bexpall -o libfunc.so
                        func.o
                     xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -brtl -o mytest main.o -L.
                        -lfunc
   COMPILER LEVEL:   XL C/C++ Enterprise Edition V7.0 for AIX
   OS LEVEL:         AIX 5.2
   DESCRIPTION:
   
   The compiler is complaining that it couldn't find the file
   libfunc.a.  Here are the compile commands and the output being
   seen:
   
   $ make OPT=-qipa
           xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -c main.c
           xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -c func.c
           xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -G -bexpall -o libfunc.so func.o
           xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -brtl -o mytest main.o -L. -lfunc
   1586-404 (E) Archive library file "libfunc.a" not found.
   1586-206 (S) Unresolved reference to symbol "func".
   1586-204 (S) Unresolved references to objects are detected.
   1586-341 (U) Code generation was not performed due to
   previously detected errors.
   Object file not created.
   make: The error code from the last command is 1.
   
   
   The third compile line creates libfunc.so, but the fourth
   line says that it can't find it.
   
   Since the error message states that it can't find libfunc.a
   instead of libfunc.so, it appears that only .a files are being
   being searched for instead of both .so and .a files.
   
   This code compiles successfully if IPA is not specified. See
   the "EXPECTED OUTPUT" section below for the output when IPA is
   not specified.
   
   
   TESTCASE:
   
   ********** main.c **********
   int main() { func(); }
   
   ********** func.c **********
   int func() {}
   
   ********** makefile **********
   XLC=xlc
   
   all:
           $(XLC) -qpdf1 $(OPT) -c main.c
           $(XLC) -qpdf1 $(OPT) -c func.c
           $(XLC) -qpdf1 $(OPT) -G -bexpall -o libfunc.so func.o
           $(XLC) -qpdf1 $(OPT) -brtl -o mytest main.o -L. -lfunc
   
   clean:
           rm -f func.o libfunc.so main.o ._pdf mytest
   
   $
   ******************************
   
   
   
   WORKAROUND:
   
   The testcase compiles successfully when -qipa is not used:
   
   $ make
           xlc -qpdf1  -c main.c
           xlc -qpdf1  -c func.c
           xlc -qpdf1  -G -bexpall -o libfunc.so func.o
           xlc -qpdf1  -brtl -o mytest main.o -L. -lfunc
   
   
   
   ACTUAL OUTPUT:
   
   $ make OPT=-qipa
           xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -c main.c
           xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -c func.c
           xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -G -bexpall -o libfunc.so func.o
           xlc -qpdf1 -qipa -brtl -o mytest main.o -L. -lfunc
   1586-404 (E) Archive library file "libfunc.a" not found.
   1586-206 (S) Unresolved reference to symbol "func".
   1586-204 (S) Unresolved references to objects are detected.
   1586-341 (U) Code generation was not performed due to previously
   detected errors.
   Object file not created.
   make: The error code from the last command is 1.
   
   
   EXPECTED OUTPUT:
   
   The testcase compiles successfully when -qipa is not used:
   
   $ make
           xlc -qpdf1  -c main.c
           xlc -qpdf1  -c func.c
           xlc -qpdf1  -G -bexpall -o libfunc.so func.o
           xlc -qpdf1  -brtl -o mytest main.o -L. -lfunc
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX
 *  The problem does not occur if -qipa is not specified.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  same as submitter's text
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  This problem has been fixed by Development.  The fix should be
   included in the next PTF of the XL C/C++ Enterprise Edition V7.0
   for AIX compiler.

title: IBM PI19997: DB2 ADMIN INSTALLING V11.1 MISSING ISPF LOAD LIBRARY IN A0CUSTXX JOB - United States
text:
z/os  A FIX IS AVAILABLE
Obtain the fix for this APAR.


SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  While installing DB2 Admin V11.1 on a system where the ISPF
   libraries are NOT in the linklist, enter the ISPF load library
   in the ISPF LLIB1 field in the LPAR parameters and leave the
   link list library blank (because do not have a link list to
   use). As a result, the A0CUSTxx job generates without a
   ISPLLIB DD which causes the job to fail, but the job STILL
   ends with an RC=0. There are two items:
   1) If an error in the A0CUSTxx job (in this case it was an
      RC -3), the overall job should end with a non-warning return
      code (RC >= 8).
   2) The description of the link list library value on the LPAR
      Parameters panel describes this value as the value of the
      link list library which is OK but the help for the ISPF
      LLIB1 field on the same panel is described as the load
      library value if not in the link list which is true but it
      wasn't used.
   The template ADBCUST in SADBDENU shows the value checked as
   being the link list library name and not the ISPF LLIB1 (or
   ISPF LLIB2 for that matter). This is the cause of the ISPF
   load lib missing from the generated job.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX
 *  n/a
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: Users of the DB2 Administration Tool for     *
   *                 z/OS and IBM Tools Customizer for z/OS.      *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: When the following LPAR Parameters      *
   *                      'ISPF Llib1' and/or 'ISPF Llib2' are    *
   *                      specified (generally if ISPF is not in  *
   *                      Linklist), submission of the generated  *
   *                      job template ADBCUST ends with          *
   *                      RC=0 / Return Code 0.  However,         *
   *                      the ADBCUST job output shows that it    *
   *                      actually failed with RC=-3 / Return     *
   *                      Code -3 due to an ISPF environment      *
   *                      not being available.  Hence, no         *
   *                      processing / update to Customization    *
   *                      table ADBTPARM took place.              *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   When the following LPAR Parameters 'ISPF Llib1' and/or
   'ISPF Llib2' are specified (generally if ISPF is not in
   Linklist), submission of the generated job template
   ADBCUST endswith RC=0 / Return Code 0.  However, ADBCUST
   job output shows that it actually failed with RC=-3 /
   Return Code -3 due to an ISPF environment not being
   available.  Hence, no processing / update to
   Customization table ADBTPARM took place.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Problem has been resolved with the following fixes:
   
   1.  Fixed error handling of rc=-3 and insured that job
   template ADBCUST returns the following error message:
   
   RC=-3: Processing of job template ADBCUST
   failed due to ISPF environment not available or ISPF
   not in Linklist, hence the reason this job ends with
   a misleading MAXCC=0000.
   
   To resolve, please check panel CCQPLPR 'LPAR Parameters'
   and ensure a valid ISPF Load Library is specified.
   
   2.  Removed the following three misleading parameters from
   panel CCQPLPR 'LPAR Parameters':
   
   - Link list library
   - ISPF Llib1
   - ISPF Llib2
   
   and replaced them with one intuitive parameter 'Load library'
   with the following field help information:
   
   CCQY004I Enter the ISPF Load library. This library will be
   used by the Tools Customizer generated batch jobs where
   applicable. Note: Specifying the ISPF Load library is optional
   if ISPF is already available in Link List.

text:

SUBSCRIBE

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  If RI relationship is involved in DELETE statement, the DELETE
   statement could hit DSNIRELF 5012 abend due to CTCUBPT = 0.
   CTCUBPT could be set to zeros after locking escalation.
   
   Customer is able to see the lock escalation message right
   before the abend.
   --
   STC89703 00000281  DSNI031I  -DB2 DSNILKES - LOCK ESCALATION
   HAS 215
        215 00000081  OCCURRED FOR
        215 00000081    RESOURCE NAME = TESTDB.TESTTS
        215 00000081    LOCK STATE =  X
        215 00000081    PLAN NAME : PACKAGE NAME = DISTSERV :
   SYSLH200
        215 00000081    COLLECTION-ID = NULLID
        215 00000081    STATEMENT NUMBER = 00000001
        215 00000081    CORRELATION-ID = db2jcc_appli
        215 00000081    CONNECTION-ID = SERVER
        215 00000081    LUW-ID = GAE9706A.OF02.CE8E7ADAD21C
        215 00000081    THREAD-INFO =
        215 00000081  TMASA03:lsrv3042.linux.rab:TMASA03:db2j
   --
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX
 *  try to avoid lock escalation.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All DB2 Z/OS V10 and V11 Delete Cascade      *
   *                 users.                                       *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: Abends04E RC00c90101 DSNIRELF:5012      *
   *                      could occur during a Delete with a      *
   *                      RI relationship on a child table        *
   *                      with the delete rule of CASCADE.        *
   *                      The delete cascade on the child         *
   *                      table could cause lock escalation.      *
   *                      During lock escalation processing,      *
   *                      DB2 may need to access SYSSTRINGS       *
   *                      to translate the child table name,      *
   *                      DB2 would free the resources for        *
   *                      this access and the CTCUBPT was         *
   *                      zeroed out in the clean-up process.     *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   After lock escalation processing, DB2 detected a zero CTCUBPT
   where it was not expected, so DB2 issued DSNIRELF:5012 abend.

   lock escalation code.

title: IBM PI81386: SERIALIZATION PROBLEM BETWEEN DBFILQS0 AND DBFHEMH0. - United States
text:
z/os  A FIX IS AVAILABLE
Obtain the fix for this APAR.


SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  We are using Shared EMHQ and IETR for FP transactions..
   Just after IMS Cold Start, IMS CTL TCB entered infinite loop
   between DFSICIO0 and BRFTDD00 (IETR).
   This is because EMHB had EMHBIVI flag on for input processing,
   but CNT had CNTFF1I and CNTFF1SQ flags on for output processing.
   This is wrong combination.
   There was serialization problem between DBFILSQ0 and BRFTDDxx
   modules (IETR). At this time, IETR module was wrong. But same
   serialization problem exists between DBFILQS0 and DBFHEMH0 too,
   because DBFILQS0 runs under SQ2 TCB while DBFHEMH0 runs under
   CTL TCB. Both modules can update EMHB address on CTBFPTBA
   concurrently.
   There are next concerns.
   1. Compare Swap (CS) should be used when update CTBFPTBA.
   2. EMHBOVI flag need to be set before updating CTBFPTBA by
     DBFILQS0.
   3. DBFILQS0 is missing to obtain DBFEMHBL latch in share mode
     when updating CTBFPTBA.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:                                              *
   * IMSFP V14 Shared EMH users                                   *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:                                         *
   * Forward Fit of PI81349 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PI81349]:                                      *
   * Shared EMH Inform server does not serialize access when      *
   * updating EMHB pointer in CTBFPTBA.                           *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   * INSTALL CORRECTIVE SERVICE FOR APAR/PTF                      *
   ****************************************************************
   This loop problem was caused by IETR changing CTBFPTBA EMHB
   pointer regardless whether there was an EMHB with message
   pending.  IETR has been changed to not overlay CTBFPTBA when an
   EMHB has EMHBIVI or EMHBOVI set.
   -----
   DBFILQS0 does not serialize CTBFPTBA update when setting EMHB
   that it obtained for inform.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  GEN:
   KEYWORDS:
   
   *** END IMS KEYWORDS ***
   DBFEMHB and DBFILQS0 have been modified to address serialized
   access when updating CTBFPTBA:
   
   DBFEMHB:
   Add 4 EMHB trace entries: EMHBRTBB-EMHBRTBE
   
   DBFILQS0:
   Shared EMH Inform Queue Server, DBFILQS0, has been modified to
   preset EMHBIVI by DBFIQLS0 before attempting to queue
   the EMHB that it obtained for inform process.
   
   DBFILQS0 uses a compare-and-swap instruction to serialize
   CTBFPTBA to set the EMHB that it obtained for inform process.
   If another task has updated CTBFPTBA with another EMHB, then it
   would release the EMHB that it obtained and continue with
   the inform process using the existing EMHB on CTBFPTBA.   The
   shared EMH output message will be processed after the
   pending input message has completed its message processing.
   
   
    
   
   

TEMPORARY FIX

title: IBM PI93279: Deleted cluster queues may become active as a result of refreshing full repository queue managers - United States
text:
z/os  A FIX IS AVAILABLE
Obtain the fix for this APAR.


SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  A Cluster queue which has been deleted from the cluster by
   setting the CLUSTER or CLUSNL attributes to (' '), can re-appear
   in the cluster configuration during a REFRESH CLUSTER operation
   issued against a full repositories for given cluster(s).
   
   This problem can be observed by its existence in the outputs of
   the MQSC display commands and seeing the 'deleted' queue
   referenced when it should not be.
   
   Due to timing windows caused by overlapping REFRESH CLUSTER
   commands (or at least, the flow of data originating from them)
   the problem may not always arise such that the deleted queue
   remains deleted in configuration.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of IBM MQ for z/OS Version 9       *
   *                 Release 0 Modification 0                     *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: Issuing a REFRESH CLUSTER command may   *
   *                      cause a deleted cluster object to be    *
   *                      republished as live to other queue      *
   *                      managers in the cluster.                *
   ****************************************************************
   The cluster cache record for an object is marked as deleted when
   the cluster is removed from the CLUSTER attribute or CLUSTERNL.
   However in some timing windows, when multiple REFRESH CLUSTER
   commands are issued in a short period, a deleted cluster Q cache
   record may be republished as live to other QMGRs in the cluster.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Republish logic for the REFRESH CLUSTER command has been
   corrected, to prevent deleted records being republished as live.
   
   
    
   
   

TEMPORARY FIX

title: IBM PK01725: ABEND0C4 IN DFSOCM30 DURING IMS SHUTDOWN - United States
text:
SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  ABEND0C4 in DFSOCM30 caused by the timing of events driven
   during shutdown.  A /CHE FREEZE command causes an SCI
   deregistration (dereg) call.  Before the SCI dereg, a /DBR
   command comes in and an AWE is sent to IMS from SCI.  The
   dereg process cleans up storage which is being used by the
   /DBR command.  Therefore, we hit an ABEND0C4.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: IMS/ESA rel 910 users who use SCI and OM.    *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: ABEND0C4 in DFSOCM30 during IMS         *
   *                      shutdown.                               *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION: INSTALL CORRECTIVE SERVICE FOR APAR/PTF      *
   ****************************************************************
   A /CHE FREEZE command was entered and shortly thereafter a /DBR
   command came in through the SPOC.  The processing of the /DBR
   command was passed into the control region and had already
   acquired some CSA storage when suddenly that storage was freed
   causing the abend when access to it was made.
   
   The storage was freed because the /CHE FREEZE shutdown process
   had reached the point in which it makes a degregister calls to
   SCI, OM and RM.  These calls resulted in the CSA storage being
   freed.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  AIDS: RIDS/SYS RIDS/CNTRL SYS CNTRL
     DEP: NONE
     GEN:
   
   *** END IMS KEYWORDS ***
   An orderly synchronization of shutdown has been established in
   the control region when commands can be entered from the SPOC
   via OM and SCI.  This synchronization provides a counter of
   active OM commands in the system, and logic in the shutdown
   process to only issue the SCI, OM and RM deregistration calls
   when the counter has reached zero.  In addition a fence is
   established to prevent further commands.
   
   The following parts have been changed:
   
   DFSSXIN0 - this is the SCI Input Exit for IMS. It receives
              control when an IMSplex member issues a request to
              be processed by IMS.  If it is an OM request and
              neither the shutdown-fence flag nor the shutdown-
              needs-posting flag is on, it increments the active
              OM command counter before proceeding with the
              request.  If either flag is on, it immediately
              returns with a return code of of IRC_ENVIRON
              and a reason code of IRSN_SHUTDOWN to OM if
              IMS is shutting down when the command is received.
   
   DFSOCM00 - this is the router module for OM-originated IMS
              commands.  When it receives a request from DFSSXIN0
              and the SCDPTRM0 flag is on, the command is ignored,
              the counter is decremented, and if the counter has
              gone to zero, shutdown is posted.  This module then
              waits for next request.
              If the flag is not on, the command is passed to the
              command action module.  Upon return the counter is
              decremented and if it has gone to zero and the
              SCDPTRM0 flag is on, this module IPOSTs shutdown
              and waits for next request.
   
   DFSOCM10 - this is the router module for OM-originated IMSplex
              commands.  When it receives a request from DFSSXIN0
              and the SCDPTRM0 flag is on, the command is ignored,
              the counter is decremented, and if the counter has
              gone to zero, shutdown is posted.  This module then
              waits for next request.
              If the flag is not on, the command is passed to the
              command action module.  Upon return the counter is
              decremented and if it has gone to zero and the
              SCDPTRM0 flag is on, this module IPOSTs shutdown
              and waits for next request.
   
   
   DFSTERM0 - this is the control task termination module.  It
              has been changed to only issue the deregistration
              calls if the count is zero and after it has set
              on the fence bit to prevent further commands.  If
              the count is not zero when it reaches this point,
              it sets the bit to request POSTing and then IWAITs.
              When posted it sets the fence bit and proceeds
              with shutdown.
   
   ISCD     - adds a new field, DFSOMCCT, to contain the count of
              active OM commands.  In the hi-order byte of this
              field, a flag byte is defined which contains two
              flag-bits: SCDDREGD, which indicates that dereg
              calls have been made, and SCDPTRM0, which indicates
              that shutdown needs to be posted when the count
              reaches zero.

title: IBM PK36738: CLUSTER STATUS IS INCORRECTLY SET TO STOPPED SHORTLY AFTER THE REQUEST TO STOP WAS MADE, INSTEAD OF BEING SET TO PARTIAL STOP - United States
text:
SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  Cluster status is incorrectly being set to stopped shortly after
   the request to stop was made, instead of being set to partial
   stop.
   
   The cluster state should be partial stop after the request is
   issued, and turn to
   stopped only after all cluster members have gone down.
   
   For ex:
   
   IF a java client is used to connect to websphere and get the
   status of the cluster, The java client reports the following:
   
   
   2006-11-29 07:49:10 INFO  root - State:
   websphere.cluster.stopped
   
   Server log reports to be stopped at:
   
   [29.11.06 07:49:40:374 CET] 00000017 ServerCollabo A
   WSVR0024I:
   Server dms.a.1.as91042.1 stopped.
   
   
   There is a 30 seconds delay.This is because the incorrect
   cluster status been set to stop.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX
 *  n/a
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: Websphere Application Server version 6.0.2   *
   *                 clustering users.                            *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: Cluster status is incorrectly set to    *
   *                      stopped shortly after a stopCluster is  *
   *                      issued.                                 *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   Cluster status is incorrectly being set to stopped shortly
   after the request to stop was made, instead of being set to
   partial stop.
   
   The cluster state should be partial stop after the request is
   issued, and turn to stopped only after all cluster members
   have gone down.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Code was rewritten to correctly set the cluster state to
   partial stop and only set the state to stopped if all cluster
   members are down.
   
   This fix only applies to version 6.0.2, it is already present
   in the GA version 6.1 code.
   
   The fix for this APAR is currently targeted for inclusion
   in fixpack 6.0.2.19.
   Please refer to the recommended updates page for delivery
   information:
   http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27004980 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27004980]

title: IBM PK70480: CLUSTER QMGR IS NOT SELECTED AFTER SUSPEND QMGR CLUSTER AND THE NEXT RESTART OF MQ WITH DEFINE REPLACE CHANNEL IN CSQINP2 - United States
text:
z/os  A FIX IS AVAILABLE
Obtain the fix for this APAR.


SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  Customer use cluster workload exit and expected the WLM exit
   select QMGR in a round-robin manner. But it does not work.
   Environment:
    FMQ0 (WMQ V6.0 on z/OS V1R7) FMQX (WMQ V5.3.1 on z/OS V1R7)
     Full repository              Full repository
     REPOSNL(FMQCLTNL)            REPOSNL(FMQCLTNL)
     NAMELIST FMQCLTNL            NAMELIST FMQCLTNL
     FMQCLT01,FMQCLT02,FMQCLT03   FMQCLT01,FMQCLT02,FMQCLT03
     Cluster queue CLQ03          Cluster Queue CLQ03
      in cluster FMQCLT03          in cluster FMQCLT03
    FMQNAGO (WMQ V5.3 FP9  on Linux)
    Partial repository
    PUT message to CLQ03 in cluster FMQCLT03
   .
   Operation :
    1. Setup the above cluster
    2. FMQ0 SUSPEND QMGR CLUSTER(FMQCLT01)
    3. FMQ0 SUSPEND QMGR CLUSTER(FMQCLT02)
    4. Check QMGR FMQO is not suspened in cluster FMQCLT03
       FMQ0DIS CLUSQMGR(FMQ0) SUSPEND shows
        CLUSQMGR(FMQ0) CLUSTER(FMQCLT01) SUSPEND(YES)
        CLUSQMGR(FMQ0) CLUSTER(FMQCLT02) SUSPEND(YES)
        CLUSQMGR(FMQ0) CLUSTER(FMQCLT03) SUSPEND(NO)
        CLUSQMGR(FMQ0) is not suspened in CLUSTER(FMQCLT03) so
        user expected FMQO is selected as target qmgr.
    5. Stop CHINIT
    6. Start CHINIT
       *Note*
       CSQINP2 contains DEFINE REPLACE CHANNEL(FMQCNLX0.TO.FMQ0)
    7. PUT message to cluster queue CLQ03 from FMQNAGO.
       All message is put to CLQ03 on FMQX.
   .
   The reason of QMGR FMQO is not select is that CLQMGR flag shows
   it is not Joined eventhough Cluster(FMQCLT03) has Joined falg.
   .
   verbx csqxdprd 'subsys=FMQO,clus=1' shows
    CLQMGR.
     Qm(FMQ0
     Flags(Local Repos CLUSRCVR-Def In-Use )
     Cluster(FMQCLT01                 )
      Flags(Local Repos CLUSRCVR-Def )
     Cluster(FMQCLT03                 )
      Flags(Local Repos CLUSRCVR-Def Joined )
     Cluster(FMQCLT02                 )
      Flags(Local Repos CLUSRCVR-Def )
   .
   The Joined ( rfxQmgrFlags_JOINED_CLUSTER ) flag should be ON if
   there is a least one cluster with Joined flag.
   The problem is the loss of the rfxQmgrFlags_JOINED_CLUSTER
   flag in the RFXCLUSTER_Q_MGR Flags field in the fastnet cache
   when the CLUSRCVR channel for the QMGR is DEFINE REPLACEd in
   CSQINP2.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX
 *  REFRESH CLUSTER or RESUME QMGR CLUSTER(FMQCLT03) will be bypass
   the problem until next restart of MQ.
   Or
   Remove DEFINE REPLACE CHANNEL of the CLUSRCVR
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of WebSphere MQ for z/OS Version 6 *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: After ALTER/DEFINE of a CLUSRCVR        *
   *                      channel using a CLUSNL when the first   *
   *                      cluster in the namelist has been        *
   *                      suspended, the MQQMF_AVAILABLE value in *
   *                      the MQWDR passed to a cluster workload  *
   *                      exit may be incorrectly set causing the *
   *                      exit to make incorrect decisions.       *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   When a CLUSRCVR channel is defined in more than one cluster
   using a CLUSNL if the FIRST cluster is suspended using SUSPEND
   QMGR CLUSTER(x) and while the CHINIT is down the CLUSRCVR
   channel is ALTERed (say to change the batch size - or even via a
   DEFINE REPLACE command in CSQINP2) then when the CHINIT is
   subsequently started during reconciliation processing in
   rrmRecoClqMgr the rfxQmgrFlags_JOINED_CLUSTER flag in the
   RFXCLUSTER_Q_MGR Flags field is incorrectly set OFF.
   This flag is redefined as MQQMF_AVAILABLE in the MQWDR and
   therefore may cause a customer cluster workload exit to
   incorrectly route messages if it relies on this flag.
   A REFRESH CLUSTER command will correct the flag, but the effect
   lasts only until the next ALTER of the CLUSRCVR channel (or QMGR
   restart if a DEFINE REPLACE for the channel exists in CSQINP2).
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  In module CSQXRRMF:
   Routine rrmChangeClqMgr has been changed to correctly set the
   rfxQmgrFlags_JOINED_CLUSTER flag in the requested ClusQMgr
   passed to rrmRecoClqMgr.
   Distributed Apars IZ14977 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IZ14977] and IZ36482 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IZ36482] have been ported to
   rrmRecoClqMgr.
   Routine rrmRecoClqMgr has been changed to correctly set the
   flag rfxQmgrFlags_JOINED_CLUSTER in the ClqMgr entry if any of
   the Clus entries have the flag set.
   This ensures that the MQQMF_AVAILABLE value in the MQWDR will
   be correctly set for use by Cluster Workload Exits.
   000Y
   CSQXRRMF
   
   
    
   
   

TEMPORARY FIX

title: IBM PK91036: LOAD PARTITION PARALLELISM UTILITY JOB ABENDC03 WITH MESSAGE DSNU1036I AND RC=8 - United States
text:
z/os  A FIX IS AVAILABLE
Obtain the fix for this APAR.


SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  a LOAD PARTITION PARALLELISM utility job failed with ABENDC03
   and MSGDSNU1036I when the INDDN data set for the INTO TABLE PART
   x statement was a DUMMY data set and the template for DISCARDDN
   doesn't have SPACE keyword.
   
   DSNU1036I   174 10:08:17.38 DSNURELD - UNABLE TO ESTIMATE SPACE
   REQUIREMENTS FOR DISCARDDN
   DSNU012I    174 10:08:19.07 DSNUGBAC - UTILITY EXECUTION
   TERMINATED, HIGHEST RETURN CODE=8
   
   DB2PARALL/K
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All DB2 9 for z/OS utility users of LOAD     *
   *                 with partition parallelism.                  *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: ABENDC03 after a LOAD with partition    *
   *                      parallelism ended with RC8 and message  *
   *                      MSGDSNU1036I - UNABLE TO ESTIMATE SPACE *
   *                      REQUIREMENTS FOR DISCARDDN.  Some of    *
   *                      the SYSREC data sets were defined as DD *
   *                      DUMMY and the DISCARD data sets were    *
   *                      dynamically allocated using TEMPLATES   *
   *                      without SPACE parameters.               *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION: Apply corrective PTF when available          *
   ****************************************************************
   A LOAD with multiple INTO TABLE PART x INDDN SYSRECnn
   DISCARDDN DISCn statements where some of the SYSREC data sets
   were defined as DD Dummy, and TEMPLATES were used for the
   DISCARD data sets with no SPACE attributes, ended with RC8.
   MSGDSNU1036I - UNABLE TO ESTIMATE SPACE REQUIREMENTS FOR
   DISCARDDN was issued.  An ABENDSC03 followed.
   
   During LOAD PARTITION PARALLELISM processing, a DD DUMMY SYSREC
   data set caused a flag to get set which indicated that no space
   estimate was available from the sysrec data set for the discard
   data set.  This led to MSGDSNU1036I and the RC8.  However,
   LOAD should tolerate the SYSREC DD DUMMY when allocating the
   DISCARD data sets.
   
   The ABENDC03 was issued because this error condition left
   some of the data sets opened.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  LOAD PARTITION PARALLELISM code has been modified to tolerate
   SYSREC DD DUMMY data sets.
   
   
    
   
   

TEMPORARY FIX

   As can be seen, this header contains multiple HTTP/1.1, Server,
   and Date header lines which is not according to RFC 2616.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of the WebSphere HTTP Server for   *
   *                 OS/390 and z/OS that write non-nph           *
   *                 (No Parse Headers) CGIs that use the         *
   *                 cgiutils module to set headers.              *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: Customer uses the cgiutils module in a  *
   *                      CGI and gets duplicate headers.         *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   The customer is using the cgiutils module in a non-nph CGI.
   The cgiutils module creates a full set of response headers for
   a nph (No Parse Headers) CGI.  A nph CGI response is passed
   through the HTTP Server with no action by the HTTP Server on
   either the response headers or content body.
   When used with a non-nph CGI both the cgiutils module and the
   HTTP Server create headers, thereby causing some duplicate
   headers.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Changed the code in the cgiutils module to recognize when it is
   called in a non-nph (No Parse Headers) CGI so that ONLY the
   headers requested are created.
   -
   Prior to this APAR if -status was set by the cgiutils module
   the following response headers were generated automatically:
       HTTP/1.1 200 OK
       MIME-Version: 1.0
       Server: IBM HTTP Server/V5R3M0
       Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2004 21:06:17 GMT
   After application of this APAR these headers will ONLY BE
   generated automatically if the CGI to be executed is prefixed
   with "nph-".
   
   The following COMPID is affected by these changes:
   
   5697D4300 HTTP Server for OS/390 and z/OS  Version 5
   
   PTF04C
   The code changes are stored in CMVC under defect PQ84618.

   --------------------------------------------------------------
   HTTP Server Planning, Installing and Using
   Part 7. Appendixes

   --------------------------------------------------------------
   Please replace:
   Note: If you want to supply your own no-parse header (nph)
   programs specifically to return your own return values, the
   name of the program must begin with nph-.  This prevents the
   server header from overriding your return value with the
   standard server return value.
   -
   with the following:
   Note: If you want to supply your own no-parse header (nph)
   programs specifically to return your own return values, the
   name of the program must begin with nph-.  This causes the
   HTTP Server to act as a pass-through mechanism from the nph
   CGI to the browser.  The HTTP Server will create no headers

    -
   A nph CGI must create both response headers and response body

   If you use the cgiutils command inside a non-nph CGI to create

title: IBM PQ88192: A POSSIBLE INTEGRITY EXPOSURE EXISTS WHEN USING FDBR IF IMS IS RESTARTED BY ARM OR AUTOMATION AND /ERE RUNS BEFORE FDBR ENDS. - United States
text:
SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.



APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  A possible data integrity exposure exists when using FDBR.
   If IMS is restarted by ARM or automation, it is possible that
   /ERE and FDBR Recovery process could run concurrently,
   resulting in damage to databases or the IMS log stream.
   No customer has seen this problem but it was verified
   internally.
   This apar will also remove the restriction that ARMRST=Y
   cannot be in effect for both the CTL region and the FDBR region.
   (Currently, specification of ARMRST=Y for FDBR disables
   ARM restart for the CTL region).
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All IMS R910 FDBR users.                     *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: A possible integrity exposure exists    *
   *                      when using FDBR if IMS is restarted by  *
   *                      arm or automation and /ERE runs before  *
   *                      FDBR ends.                              *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION: INSTALL CORRECTIVE SERVICE FOR APAR/PTF      *
   ****************************************************************
   A possible data integrity exposure exists when using FDBR.  If
   IMS is restarted by ARM (i.e. ARM=Y was specified for the IMS
   system while ARM=N was specified for the FDBR system) or user
   automation, it is possible that the /ERE of the restarted IMS
   and the FDBR recovery process could run concurrently, resulting
   in damage to databases and/or the IMS log stream.
   
   
    
   
   

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  AIDS: RIDS/SYS RIDS/CNTRL SYS CNTRL
     DEP: NONE
     GEN:
   
   *** END IMS KEYWORDS ***
   Both the IMS and FDBR systems have been modified to issue a
   global resource serialization ENQ in order to prevent a failed
   IMS system from being restarted before FDBR completes its
   recovery.
   
   When FDBR senses that the IMS system has abended, its first
   action before it begins recovery is to issue an exclusive
   global-wide ENQ using a QNAME of IMSVSFDR and a RNAME of ten
   characters consisting of the subsystem ids of the IMS and FDBR
   systems along with the IMS version number.  FDBR holds this
   ENQ until it completes the recovery.
   
   Early in an IMS restart, the system makes a TEST ENQ call using
   the same QNAME and RNAME to determine whether the resource is
   available.  If it is not, then FDBR must be in recovery and IMS
   waits for 3 seconds before retrying the TEST ENQ.  When the
   resource becomes available, IMS proceeds with its restart.
   Note that the IMS system does not ever obtain nor hold the ENQ.
   
   Because the ENQ now prevents a restarted IMS system from
   interfering with the FDBR recovery, the restriction that
   ARMRST=Y cannot be in effect for both the IMS system and the
   FDBR region simultaneously is removed.  Previously, an ARMRST=Y
   specification for FDBR disabled the ARM restart for the IMS
   system.  With this maintenance ARMRST=Y can be specified for
   both system and each will be restarted by ARM if it abends
   independently of the other.
   
   The following parts have been changed:
   
   DFSFDR00 - issues the ENQ for the FDBR system.
   
   DFSFDR10 - now issues the FDBR ARM Ready call, instead of
              the ARM Associate call which negated the ARMRST=Y
              setting of the IMS system.
   
   DFSRST00 - issues the TEST ENQ with a wait of 3 seconds
              between calls if the resource is not available.
   
   DFSTERM0 - issues the FDBR DEQ for the resource after the
              locks have been released and the log closed.
   
   Additional Keywords: CMDERE CMD/ERE
   
   
    
   
   

TEMPORARY FIX

title: IBM HTTP Session time-out settings and overwrite precedence rules - United States
text:
WebSphere http session management time-out wasrun precedence overwrite TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 It is possible to set the HTTP Session time-out in various places on the IBM® WebSphere® Application Server Administrative Console. It is also possible to set HTTP Session time-out for the application packaging process. 

Since Session time-out can be set in multiple places, it is necessary to understand how the ultimate Session time-out for an application is determined. 

CAUSE
Application needs HTTP session time-out set.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The HTTP Session time-out can be set in the following places: 

 * From the Administrative Console at the server, Enterprise application, and Web application levels 
 * At the time when the application is packaged 
 * In the application code


Setting the HTTP Session time-out from the Administrative Console 
1. To set the HTTP Session time-out at the server level, navigate to Servers > Application Servers > Your Server > Web Container > Session Management. 

In the Session time-out section of this window, you can select No time-out or Set time-out by clicking the appropriate radio button. If you choose to set the time-out, type the desired value in minutes in the box. 


2. To set the HTTP Session time-out at the Enterprise Application level, navigate to Applications > Enterprise Applications > Your Application > Session Management. 

Check Override in the Override Session Management section, then select to set the time-out and the time-out value. This sets the application session to overwrite those values set at the parent, which in this case is the Server level. 


3. To set the HTTP Session time-out at the Web Application level, navigate to Applications > Enterprise Applications > Your Application > Web Module > Your Web App.war > Session Management. 

Check Override in the Override Session Management section, then select to set the time-out and the time-out value. This sets the Application Session to overwrite those values set at the parent levels, which in this case is the Server or Enterprise Application level. 

After modifying these settings, save the master configuration. 

Setting HTTP Session time-out when application is packaged 

The application developer can also select to set the HTTP Session time-out parameter when the application is packaged. This value is stored in the web.xml file for the Web application. 

This setting overrides any session time-outs defined from the Administrative Console. Alter this setting by repackaging the application with a new value, or by modifying the web.xml file. The entry in the web.xml will be as follows: 
          <session-config> 
      *          <session-timeout>60</session-timeout>
 * 
 *       </session-config>

 

Where the "session-timeout" is an integer value for the desired session time-out in minutes. 
Setting HTTP Session time-out from the application code 

Finally, the HTTP Session time-out can be set in the application code. The programmer can invoke the setMaxInactiveInterval() method on HttpSession object to set the time-out value as desired. This setting overrides any time-out defined in the application package or made from the Administrative Console. 

HTTP Session time-out Override Precedence Summary 

The list below shows the precedence from which the final HTTP Session time-out is derived. 

1. Server Level [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21163875&aid=1] Lowest level 2. Enterprise Application [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21163875&aid=1] Overrides the Server Level if Override is selected 3. Web Application [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21163875&aid=1] Overrides the Server and Enterprise Application settings if Override is selected 4. Application Level (web.xml) [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21163875&aid=1] Overrides Server, Enterprise Application, and Web Application settings 5. Application Code [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21163875&aid=1] Overrides all other settings RELATED INFORMATION

title: IBM DataPower Gateways Firmware Support Lifecycle - United States
text:
datapower;support;lifecycle;support lifecycle;maintenance;firmware;release;releases;firmware releases;upgrade;upgrades;features;defect NEWS

ABSTRACT
This document provides information on the IBM DataPower Gateway Firmware Support Lifecycle.

CONTENT
IBM® DataPower® Gateway is a purpose-built gateway that provides security, traffic control, mediation and optimized access to a full range of mobile, web, application programming interface (API), service-oriented architecture (SOA), B2B and cloud workloads. It supports multi-cloud deployment and is available in Docker container, Linux application, VMware virtual machine and physical appliance form factors.

IBM provides flexible support options to meet the needs of your business and minimize any business impact. The IBM DataPower Gateways end-of-service support policy applies differently between hardware and firmware.

Hardware 

DataPower physical appliance hardware is supported for a minimum of five years, starting at the General Availability of the new product. Beginning with the 8436 models, standard appliance service and support is available for five years from the end-of-marketing (EOM) date as described in the IBM Appliance Support Handbook [http://www.ibm.com/support/customercare/sas/f/applhandbook/home.html].

For end-of-service information on physical appliances, see IBM DataPower Gateways End of Service dates [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21317845]. 

Firmware 

Businesses are building modernized digital platforms to drive innovation and disruption within the industry. IBM DataPower Gateways are a core component in these platforms and it needs to deliver new business functionality to keep pace with business innovation.

Effective with DataPower Gateway firmware V7.6 [https://www.ibm.com/common/ssi/cgi-bin/ssialias?infotype=AN&subtype=CA&htmlfid=897/ENUS217-265&appname=USN], DataPower introduces a Continuous Delivery (CD) model to accelerate delivery of new capabilities and meet market needs. DataPower CD will consist of two releases:

 1. CD release approximately once per quarter  * Only the most recent CD release is supported at a given time.
    
    
 2. Long Term Support (LTS) release every 12 months.  * LTS releases are for customer seeking enhanced stability and do not wish to upgrade on the CD schedule, while CD releases are intended for customers seeking the latest features.
     * The first LTS release post 7.6 GA will be within two years. Subsequent LTS releases will occur every 12 months.
     * LTS releases will be supported for a minimum of 2 years.
    
    

Firmware V7.6 and later have no extended support plan available for any release of DataPower Gateway. IBM will publish a notice of support discontinuance (end-of-service) for a LTS releases at least 12 months before the effective date.

Firmware V7.5 and earlier will remain on the traditional IBM DataPower Gateway support model where they will be supported for a minimum of 2 years. There is no extended support plan available for any of these releases. IBM will publish a notice of support discontinuance (end-of-service) for releases at least 12 months before the effective date.

title: IBM Locating ITM Workspace Application Support Files for z/OS Agents - United States
text:
AppSupport OMEGAMON application support 350 360 410 420 610 601 700 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 This technote addresses the commonly asked question of where can workspace application support files be found for z/OS Agents. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Before you can view data collected by monitoring agents, you must install application support for the agents on the Tivoli Enterprise Portal Server and on the hub Tivoli Enterprise Monitoring Server. When you install application support on the Tivoli Enterprise Portal Server, you are installing the files required for presenting workspaces and online help for each monitoring agent. When you install application support on the hub monitoring server, you are installing the files required for product-provided situations, situation distributions, and other product-specific data. Installing application support on the hub monitoring server is also known as "seeding" the hub.
Most z/OS-based agents provide application support files on CDs or DVDs, which are separate from the mainframe installation media. Distributed agents include their application support files in the distributed installation process. Each CD /DVD that contains application support files is listed below, with information about which products use the CD /DVD and where the CD / DVD can be found. The latest level in fulfillment is the CD /DVD on this list. Where possible, IBM provides both .zip and .tar formats, as well as .iso format, so that a physical CD / DVD can be created.

Please note that the IBM Tivoli Monitoring (ITM) media is separate from the workspace application support files which are included with products that run in the ITM environment. ITM can be obtained by ordering either 5724-C04 IBM Tivoli Monitoring through Passport Advantage or the no charge 5698-A79 IBM Tivoli Management Services on z/OS through Shop zSeries. Your IBM rep can ask Techline to configure and submit the order as well. 5698-A79 includes the server, engine, and configurator on z/OS. Workspace application support files may have their own fixpacks which are separate and distinct from any ITM fixpacks. Fixpacks can be found on the product support urls at: 
http://www-306.ibm.com/software/support/index_A_Z.html [http://www-306.ibm.com/software/support/index_A_Z.html].

The ITM Configuration Guide describes the application support installation process. It can be found online in the ITM information center at: https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSTFXA_6.3.0/com.ibm.itm.doc_6.3/install/agent_support.htm [https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSTFXA_6.3.0/com.ibm.itm.doc_6.3/install/agent_support.htm]. A useful reference for this activity is a technote that lists all of the ITM product code. It can be found at:
http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21265222 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21265222].

title: IBM Advanced date queries for Maximo (Oracle) - United States
text:
querying; qbe; TPAEORACLE TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Users often want to query records based on fixed date ranges, such as "Last 7 days" or "This week". This shows examples of SQL syntax that can be added to a where clause to do this. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM

Users often want to query records based on fixed date ranges, such as "Last 7 days" or "This week" without having to enter dates every time. This shows SQL syntax that can be added to any where clause to do this dynamically. 

For Oracle: 

 

Records with a date within the last seven days to the second. Change datecolumn to the appropriate column for the table: 

 AND (datecolumn BETWEEN SYSDATE-7 AND SYSDATE) 

 

Records with a date within the last seven calendar days (the TRUNC function cuts off the time component, effectively setting it to midnight): 

 AND (datecolumn BETWEEN TRUNC(SYSDATE-7) AND SYSDATE) 

 

 

Changing the 7 to 30 in the above conditions to query for the last 30 days. 

 

Records with a date within the last seven days to the second. Change datecolumn to the appropriate column for the table: 

 AND (datecolumn BETWEEN SYSDATE-30 AND SYSDATE) 

 

Records with a date within the last seven calendar days (the TRUNC function cuts off the time component, effectively setting it to midnight): 

 AND (datecolumn BETWEEN TRUNC(SYSDATE-30) AND SYSDATE) 

 

 

It gets a little tricky, but you can also use this type of condition to select by a specific calendar week (Sun - Sat) instead of 7 days prior to today: 

 

Records with a datecolumn value that falls within the current week, where the week starts with Sunday: 

 AND (datecolumn BETWEEN (TRUNC(SYSDATE - (TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'D')-1))) AND SYSDATE) 

 

Records with a datecolumnvalue that falls within the previous week, from Sunday through Saturday midnight: 

 AND (datecolumn BETWEEN (TRUNC(SYSDATE - (TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'D')+6))) AND (TRUNC(SYSDATE - (TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'D')-1)))) 

 

A DBA or MAXIMO Administrator can develop useful date range queries to meet the users' needs, and make them available as public saved queries in the various applications' query screens. Users can then pick date queries and enhance them to add personal criteria, such as ENTEREDBY, SUPERVISOR, etc. and save them as their own.

title: IBM Differences between 'import ' and 'access' stereotypes on dependency lines between packages in IBM Rational Tau - United States
text:
TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How does 'import ' differ from 'access' stereotype on dependency lines between packages in IBM Rational Tau? 

ANSWER
Consider the packages X, Y, and Z. 

For example: X<<import>>Y<<import>>Z .
Import is transitive. So in the above example, X imports from Y and Y imports from Z. When we use <<import>> it means that package 'X' can use elements in package 'Z'. 

Conversely, with the example: X<<access>>Y<<access>>Z
Access is non-transitive. So in the above example, X will not be able to access any of the elements in Z. 

 

If the above does not function as expected in your environment, please contact IBM Rational Client Support for further analysis of your model.

title: IBM How to Rollback From a Fix Pack or Interim Fix to an Earlier Build - United States
text:
uninstall; revert; downgrade; hotsite; HS; out; fixpack TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 There may be times when there is a need to remove a previously installed Fix Pack or Interim Fix (hotsite) and revert to the original installed version. This document describes how to roll back an installed Fix Pack or Interim Fix applied to Cognos BI. 

ANSWER
Assuming create backup was selected, there will be a folder with the backup under the uninstall directory. Use these files to roll back. In version 10.2.1 FP1 and above there is no option to create a backup, instead backups are automatically created in the <cognos_install>/bkp directory.
Note that the backup directories only contain copies of all individual files that were modified by the fix pack or interim fix, not the entire contents of the original directory.

Care must also be taken when removing interim fixes to ensure that there weren't later interim fixes applied which also contain some of the same files. It is recommended that a full system and content store backup be performed before attempting.

Steps: 



 1. Stop the Cognos service and ensure that Cognos Configuration is not running. 
 2. When setting up the configuration of a newly installed Cognos BI environment, it is important to note that if you configure the new installation against the original content store, it is permanently upgraded to the new version and can no longer be used in the original environment. As a result, always create a backup of the content store prior to upgrading.
    If a roll back to the original version is required, you can simply restore the backup. However, any work done after the content store has been upgraded (reports, models, security, etc...) to the new version will be lost, as all of this information is saved in the content store.
    If you try to revert back to an earlier environment configured against the upgraded content store, you will get an error similar to the one below:
    CM-CFG-5027 Unable to upgrade the content store to the to the version N that is compatible with this version of Content Manager. The current version of the content store is M. 
 3. Also, please refer to the notes on the fix pack which would include perquisites on Backup/Restore of content store and also other requirements. 
 4. For versions 8 - 10.2.1: In the <cognos_install>/uninstall/backup directory there will be a list of date stamped folders with the applied fix packs and/or interim fixes. 
    For versions 10.2.1 FP1 and above: This is stored in the <cognos_install>/bkp directory 
 5. Go into the folders and check the cmplst.txt file and check for the correct version to revert to. 
 6. Once the correct version is found, copy the contents of the whole folder and paste it at the <cognos_install> level, which will overwrite the files applied by fix pack or interim fix update. 
 7. Start the Cognos service.

title: IBM After upgrading to 7.0.1.0 you get SSL error AMQ9716 - United States
text:
AMQ9716 7.0.1.0 SSL OCSP SSL TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You upgrade to WebSphere MQ 7.0.1.0 (or later) and have SSL enabled channels. After the upgrade you notice that in the Queue Manager error LOGs you see the following error message:

AMQ9716: Remote SSL certificate revocation status check failed for channel '????'. 
The channel does not start. 

SYMPTOM
Error AMQ9716


CAUSE
With the release of WebSphere MQ V7.0.1.0 the use of OCSP certificate revocation checking was included. With this new feature, most likely your SSL certificates have a OCSP AuthorityInfoAccess (AIA) certificate extension embedded inside them. 


This was ignored before V7.0.1.0. Now it is being used to verify the certificate. The most likely cause of the failure is that the system can not access the servers listed in the AIA. This then returns a UNKNOWN status when the check is done. The default action for MQ is to not allow the channel to start and the AMQ9716 to be reported when the UNKNOWN is returned.


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The best thing to do in this case is to determine the cause of the UNKNOWN return code and fix it. 


There are two possible methods to discover which OCSP AuthorityInfoAccess URL is embedded in a certificate. 

Method 1.
Place the certificate on a Windows machine; ensure to use a file extension of "crt" and double-click it. View the detail extensions for the AIA. 

[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21399255&aid=1]

Method 2
Use IBM Key Management (gskit) GUI to view them. Issue the following command::
In Windows: strmqikm 
In UNIX: gsk7ikm (MQ V7) or runmqckm (MQ V8)

From the IBM Key Management window:
Select View/Edit for certificate
View Details
Extensions
AuthorityInfoAccess

[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21399255&aid=2]

The first step would be to insure that connection to the URL in your certificate can be reached.


Work-around:
Use this only as a temporary fix until the root cause can be found.
You can do the following. It will still do OCSP checking and if REVOKED is returned then the channel will not start. A GOOD return code will allow the channel to start. If UNKNOWN is returned it will not stop the channel from starting and the AMQ9716 will not be reported.

UNIX and Linux systems add the following to qm.ini
SSL:
OCSPAuthentication=OPTIONAL

To set for a Windows Queue Manager, run the following command:
amqmdain reg YourQMgrName -c add -s SSL -v OCSPAuthentication=OPTIONAL

The OCSPAuthentication setting is also applicable to clients and can also be set in the client ini file (e.g. mqclient.ini). Changes to the client OCSPAuthentication setting will take effect after the application is restarted.

On a queue manager, users will need to issue a REFRESH SECURITY TYPE(SSL) command (or the GUI/PCF equivalent) in order for the change in SSL settings to take effect.

OCSP provides your SSL channels with additional security. Once the cause of the AMQ9716 error has been addressed then you are strongly recommended to re-enable OCSP enforcement

RELATED INFORMATION
 OCSP Info [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSFKSJ_7.1.0/com.ibm.mq.doc/sy13000_.htm?lang=en]


 

PRODUCT ALIAS/SYNONYM

title: IBM How to export and import keys from an HSM-enabled IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance - United States
text:
TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How do I export and import private keys between the same or different Hardware Security Module (HSM) enabled IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance? 

ANSWER
HSM-enabled DataPower appliances support the export of private keys using the crypto-export command. For key export to work, various conditions must be met: 

 * HSMs must be initialized and in the same key sharing domain on exporting and importing machines 
 * The private key in question must be marked exportable at keygen time (see keygen's exportable option) 
 * HSMs on exporting and importing machines must share internal key-wrapping keys (see hsm-clone-kwk command). A key-wrapping key is a key that encrypts another key.


Each HSM has a special key inside of it, the key-wrapping key, that is used to encrypt exported private keys (and to decrypt imported private keys). If the goal is to restore exported keys to the same appliance, then you don't need to worry about hsm-clone-kwk, red keys, or the hsm-domain parameter. That is because the key-wrapping key at import time will already match the key-wrapping key at export time (since the HSM device is the same). If the goal is to move exported keys from one appliance to another one, then all of the steps in this section must be followed :- 

First, the two HSMs in question must be both be initialized and in the same key sharing domain. This means that they must both be initialized in the same mode (both in Security Level 2 or both in Security Level 3). In Security Level 2 mode, they must have used the same hsm-domain parameter during hsm-reinit (this parameter has a default value that is the same on all appliances). In Security Level 3 mode, they must have used the same red PED key during hsm-reinit (and the second initialization must not have overwritten the key value from the first initialization). 

Second, the key to be exported must be exportable. The exportability of keys is immutable. It is determined at keygen time, and it is controlled by that command's exportable parameter. If a key was created outside of the appliance (not using keygen), then it is always considered exportable. 

Finally, before the crypto-export crypto-import sequence, the key-wrapping keys must be synchronized using the hsm-clone-kwk command. This command must be run four times: once on the source HSM appliance (with the key-wrapping key you are copying), once on the destination HSM appliance, once again on the source HSM appliance, and once again on the destination HSM appliance. Each time the command is run, it will need the output file from the previous step (as the input to the current step) which must be moved manually (usually with the copy command). 

Once all of this has been done, then private keys may move from system to system with crypto-export and crypto-import. 

Note that the non-HSM appliance can export keys immediately at keygen time, but never at a later time. 

For additional information refer to the online Info Center [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wsdatap/v3r8m2/index.jsp?topic=%2Fxi50%2Fwelcome.htm] and search for "PIN entry device".

Note: You will need to sign into the documentation portal with your IBM Registration ID and password.

title: IBM Pasting attribute 'Object Text' to clipboard failed with error message: 'OLE problem: Command failed' for object 1 - United States
text:
export; module export TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When exporting IBM Rational DOORS module to Microsoft Word, following error occurs:
"Error pasting attribute 'Object Text' to clipboard failed with error message: 'OLE 
problem: Command failed' for object 1". 

SYMPTOM
When IBM Rational DOORS client is installed on Microsoft Windows 2003 server, and when trying to export a module to Microsoft Word, the following error occurs: 


Error pasting attribute 'Object Text' to clipboard failed with error message: 'OLE problem: Command failed' for object 1 





CAUSE
This has been identified and logged as APAR ID: PM08992 


The problem is caused by a lack of Shared Pool Memory in Microsoft Windows. When we send a very large picture to the clipboard it does get there, but the 'paste' into Word will fail if the amount of data in the clipboard is larger than the available shared pool memory. The amount of available shared pool memory that is available is configured by the OS and cannot be manually altered. 



DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
The problem only occurs when IBM Rational DOORS clients are installed on Microsoft Windows 2003 server machine 

Exporting from IBM Rational DOORS clients installed on Microsoft Windows XP exports successfully




RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Suggested Wordaround: 

 

 * On Microsoft Windows 2003 server, try exporting the module to Rich Text Format(RTF). You may then save it to .doc extension. 
 * If you have it running on VMWare, try increasing the amount of memory allocated to it.

title: IBM Why are some SQL queries slow running? - United States
text:
Informix; Performance; IC62006; TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Why do some SQL's seem to run slower prior to installing Informix Dynamic Server 11.50.xC6? 

CAUSE
You may be running into a known defect - APAR IC62006. 

This defect causes the optimizer to choose a much slower path than needed due to the incorrect calculation of the cost of the 'best' path. One way to test if this defect is impacting your queries performance is to use the 'ordered' clause as an optimizer directive "SELECT {+ explain ordered } ", this can be used as a workaround.

If you are already using 11.50.xC6 or greater and still experience slow running SQL's, you can use the following steps to help identify and narrow down the problem:
1 - Enable 'set explain;' within the query to get output of how the engine optimizes your query.
2 - Ensure update statistics has been run against all tables reference in the FROM clause, or in sub-queries.
3 - Remove one filter in the where clause to see if that makes a difference in performance of the query.
4 - Consider adding indexes to mimic join conditions within the filter.
5 - Consider using Optimizer directives to assist the optimizer in choosing the best plan/path for your query.



ANSWER
This has been identified as a product defect under APAR IC62006 fixed in 11.50.xC6 or greater

RELATED INFORMATION
 APAR number IC62006 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IC62006]

title: IBM NoClassDefFoundError running Java class selected from server plugin jar - United States
text:
wid; noclassdeffounderror; java; jar TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 The visual snippet editor allows you to search and find methods in classes available only on a restricted basis at runtime. A runtime exception occurs when the Java™ snippet calls a method in a class found in one of the plugin JARs in the server's plugins directory. 

CAUSE
Some of the Java methods found in the JARs in the server's plugin directory are available to be called, but some of them are considered internal use only and an exception is thrown if you try to call them from user code.

DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
A runtime exception is detected in the server log naming a class and method called from a visual snippet in the application.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The reason the method you selected in the snippet editor cannot be called in the JAR in the plugins directory is because of the architecture of the server. JARs in the plugins directory have a list that specifies what classes in the JAR can be called. This is called the exports list, and it is honored by the class loader the server uses. Classes not on the list are considered internal use only. Thus, not all classes in the server plugin JARs are available to be called by user code. 

You can call any method when the JAR is in the server's library directorym because it is not being treated as a plugin and a different class loader is used, one which does not implement the exports list.

The snippet editor is not aware of this mechanism so it treats a plugin JAR the same as a regular Java JAR file. That is it allows you to select the (unavailable) class and method to call in your program. The resolution is to make sure that classes you call in plugin JARs appear on the exports list. 

For example you may search for StringUtils and find the class org.apache.commons.lang.StringUtils in the WebSphere JAR plugin/com.ibm.ws.jpa.jar. This class is used internally by the plugin and it is not exported. In this case you must download the class you need directly from Apache and place the JAR in the server's classpath.

title: IBM Why are my Microsoft Office patch deployments failing? - United States
text:
129; Client; Patch; googlebigfix TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 The following document describes additional steps necessary to patch Office installations prior to Office 2007. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM


There are three different ways to deploy Office updates and patches in TEM, troubleshooting steps will vary depending on your deployment method:

 1. Administrative Installation: 

 1. The Office product being patched must be pointing to the correct administrative installation point, the admin point must match the product being patched. An Office 2000 Standard installation cannot be pointing to an Office 2000 Professional admin point. (You can reassign your admin point by using the "Office Administrative Installation Point Reassignment" task in the BES Support site.)
 2. There can only be one Office product present on the computer. Multiple installations of different Office versions is an exception. (Office 2000 Small Business and Office 2000 Professional is not supported, whereas Office 2000 Small Business and Office XP Professional is supported.)
 3. The patch must have been properly applied to the admin point before deploying the action. Click here [http://support.microsoft.com/?kbid=307783] for information from Microsoft on how to do this. 
 4. The administrative installation point must be shared with "read" permissions given to "ANONYMOUS LOGON", "NETWORK", or "EVERYONE" on a Windows NT, Windows 2000, Windows XP, or Windows 2003 system.
    
 5. Null session [https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/mydeveloperworks/wikis/home?lang=en#/wiki/Tivoli%20Endpoint%20Manager/page/Creating%20a%20Null%20Session%20Share] must be enabled for the share.

2. Network Installation: 

 1. When deploying the action, you must supply a valid UNC path (\\server_name\share_name) to the appropriate Office setup files. The shared setup files must match the product being patched, an Office 2000 Standard installation cannot be patched by providing the Office 2000 Professional setup files. 
 2. For Office 2000, there can only be one Office product present on the computer. Multiple installations of different Office versions is an exception. (Office 2000 Small Business and Office 2000 Professional is not supported, whereas Office 2000 Small Business and Office XP Professional is supported) 
 3. The Office setup files must be shared with "read" permissions given to "ANONYMOUS LOGON", "NETWORK", or "EVERYONE" on a Windows NT, Windows 2000, Windows XP, or Windows 2003 system. 
 4. Null session [https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/mydeveloperworks/wikis/home?lang=en#/wiki/Tivoli%20Endpoint%20Manager/page/Creating%20a%20Null%20Session%20Share] must be enabled for the share.

3. Local Installation: 
There are two methods of supplying a local installation cache to those endpoints that do not already have one available. Note that endpoints with a local installation cache available on disk may deploy Local Installation Fixlet messages without any other preparation: 

 1. Local CD Method: The proper Office CD matching the product being patched must be placed in the local CD-ROM drive. 
 2. Cache Distribution Method: Use the Microsoft Office Source Configuration Wizard to upload and distribute Office source files to cache locally on client computers. Once files have been cached locally, installation Fixlet messages can now be deployed.
